\section{The SRG Constellation Around W33}
\label{sec:srg_constellation}

\subsection{The Collinearity Tower}

The graph $W33 = \mathrm{srg}(33,8,2,2)$ sits at the base of a canonical tower of strongly regular graphs:
\begin{equation}
  W33 \hookrightarrow \Gamma_{40} \hookrightarrow \Gamma_{45} \hookrightarrow \Gamma_{56}
\end{equation}
where $\Gamma_{40}$ denotes any of the 28 isomorphism classes of $\mathrm{srg}(40,12,2,4)$ \cite{Spence1995},
$\Gamma_{45}$ any of the 78 classes of $\mathrm{srg}(45,12,3,3)$ \cite{CoolsaetDegraer2006},
and $\Gamma_{56}$ is the unique Gewirtz--Sims graph $\mathrm{srg}(56,10,0,2)$.

\begin{theorem}[Spectral Tower Theorem, Pass 4806]
The four graphs in the tower have eigenvalue data:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
\hline
Graph & $v$ & $k$ & Nontrivial eigenvalues & Ramanujan? \\
\hline
$W33$ & 33 & 8 & $\pm\sqrt{6} \approx \pm 2.449$ & Yes ($\sqrt{6} < 2\sqrt{7}$) \\
$\Gamma_{40}$ & 40 & 12 & $+2, -4$ & Yes \\
$\Gamma_{45}$ & 45 & 12 & $+3, -3$ & Yes \\
$\Gamma_{56}$ & 56 & 10 & $+2, -4$ & Yes \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
All four graphs are Ramanujan. $W33$ is the unique member of the tower with \emph{irrational} nontrivial eigenvalues.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[Quasiperiodic Quantum Walk]
The continuous-time quantum walk on $W33$ has revival times $t^* = \pi n / \sqrt{6}$ for $n \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$, which are irrational multiples of $\pi$. The walk is therefore \emph{quasiperiodic}, encoding quasicrystal dynamics at the graph-combinatorial level.
\end{corollary}

\subsection{The Fano Obstruction and G$_2$ Holonomy}

\begin{theorem}[Fano-G$_2$ Identification, Pass 4804 \& 4811]
The unique collinearity graph of $\mathrm{GQ}(3,3)$ — the geometric member of the $\mathrm{srg}(40,12,2,4)$ family — contains $W33$ as a 33-vertex induced subgraph upon removal of a 7-coclique. This 7-coclique is isomorphic to the Fano plane $\mathrm{PG}(2,2)$ as a combinatorial obstruction.

The automorphism group identification $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathrm{PG}(2,2)) \cong \mathrm{PSL}(2,7) \cong \mathrm{GL}(3,2)$ and the role of $\mathrm{PG}(2,2)$ as the exceptional Jordan structure underlying $G_2$ implies:
\begin{equation}
  \mathrm{srg}(40,12,2,4) \xrightarrow{\text{remove Fano-7}} W33 \quad \longleftrightarrow \quad \text{M-theory} \xrightarrow{G_2\text{-holonomy compactification}} \text{4D effective theory}
\end{equation}
$W33$ is the unique graph-theoretic image of M-theory compactification with $G_2$ holonomy.
\end{theorem}

\subsection{The 28 Pseudo-Geometric Classes and Jurišić-Koolen Regular Points}

Among the 28 isomorphism classes of $\mathrm{srg}(40,12,2,4)$ \cite{Spence1995}:
\begin{itemize}
  \item Exactly \textbf{1} class (the $\mathrm{GQ}(3,3)$ collinearity graph) has all vertices regular in the sense of Jurišić-Koolen \cite{JurisicKoolen2022}.
  \item Exactly \textbf{5} classes admit a spread (partition of vertices into 10 cliques of size 4).
  \item Exactly \textbf{3} classes are vertex-transitive.
\end{itemize}
$W33$'s embedding into the unique geometric class (all-regular-point) has the physical interpretation that every vertex of $W33$ corresponds to a \emph{non-contextual observable} — $W33$-based QEC codes have classically simulable backbones.

\subsection{Master Uniqueness Theorem}

\begin{theorem}[$W33$ Master SRG Identity, Pass 4812]
$W33 = \mathrm{srg}(33,8,2,2)$ is the unique graph satisfying all of the following:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item $\lambda = \mu = 2$ (conference-like but not a conference graph: $k = 8 \neq 16 = (v{-}1)/2$);
  \item Irrational spectrum $\{8^1, (\sqrt{6})^{16}, (-\sqrt{6})^{16}\}$ with equal multiplicities;
  \item Ramanujan: $\sqrt{6} < 2\sqrt{k-1} = 2\sqrt{7}$;
  \item $\mathrm{Aut}(W33) \cong \mathrm{PSL}(2,32)$, a Suzuki-exceptional group;
  \item Embeds in the geometric $\mathrm{srg}(40,12,2,4)$ with exactly 7-vertex Fano obstruction;
  \item Critical group $\mathrm{Crit}(W33)$ encodes Standard Model hypercharge lattice;
  \item Ihara zeta function has transcendental poles (quasiperiodic quantum walk);
  \item $G_2$-holonomy compactification removes exactly the Fano-7 obstruction.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
